note: Sat 29 Aug 2026, ~07:35 SGT weekend run (SGX/HKEX/US all closed). Latest completed US session is Friday 28 Aug close; latest completed HK/JP/KR/SG sessions in the price feed are Thursday 27 Aug (Friday's Asia bar had not yet consolidated at fetch time -- a normal lag, not a holiday). Friday's dominant, portfolio-defining event was Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish debut Jackson Hole keynote, which triggered a sharp rout in gold/silver/miners/rare earths/crypto while broad equities and credit barely reacted -- the clear #1-2 stories below. This is a genuine weekend catch-up sweep: several items are dated 26-28 Aug given the event density heading into the print, and Saturday-specific new headlines beyond the Friday-evening reaction were not found in this run's search window.

items.headline: Gold/silver/miners suffer sharpest one-day rout in months as Fed Chair Warsh turns hawkish at Jackson Hole debut
items.summary: Spot gold fell 3.14% to ~$4,456/oz (breaking below its ~$4,526 200-day MA) and silver fell 4.24% to ~$66.21/oz -- GLD -3.24% to $408.89, SLV -4.38% to $60.02 -- after Warsh's debut Jackson Hole speech reignited September rate-hike bets. Silver miners were hit hardest: First Majestic (AG) -5.09%, Hecla (HL) -4.42%, Pan American (PAAS) -3.59% intraday, becoming one of the worst-performing US sectors within 25 minutes of his remarks, after GDX had rallied roughly 40% month-to-date into the event.
items.actionable: The levered silver/miners sleeve took its largest single-day drawdown in months; treat this as a rates-driven unwind of an extremely crowded rally rather than a fundamental break, but expect elevated volatility around the September FOMC before adding fresh leverage.

items.headline: Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole debut lifts September hike odds to ~57-58%, 2yr yield and dollar jump
items.summary: In his first Jackson Hole speech as Fed Chair ("In Our Time"), Warsh said inflation is "still too high" and the Fed has "more work to do," explicitly declined to offer forward guidance ("just don't call it forward guidance -- it has overstayed its welcome"), and floated cutting FOMC meetings from 8 to 6 a year. CME-tracked September hike odds jumped from ~36% to ~57-58%, the 2-year Treasury yield rose 11.8bp to 4.348%, and the dollar index gained 0.5% within the session.
items.actionable: A genuine hawkish repricing, not just rhetoric -- keeps pressure on the levered silver/gold sleeve and duration into the September FOMC, while supporting the large cash pile's yield and SGX bank margins.

items.headline: BLS preliminary benchmark revision cuts payrolls by 79,000, a large miss versus the +183K consensus
items.summary: BLS's annual preliminary benchmark revision showed nonfarm employment through March 2026 was overstated by 79,000 (private payrolls -178,000), versus a Bloomberg-surveyed consensus for an upward revision of +183,000 -- a genuine miss in the hawkish direction, though a far smaller downward revision than the prior year's -911K. The print, released alongside Warsh's speech, reinforced the day's rate-repricing move.
items.actionable: A genuine labor-market data-quality miss that complicates the Fed's job -- watch for the final benchmark revision (due with the Jan 2027 report) as a source of continued noise around the rate path.

items.headline: Bitcoin drops ~3% below $78K on hawkish Warsh surprise; ~$481M in crypto liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin fell from above $81K to as low as $76,877 (closing -3.18% to $77,703 per the price feed) after Warsh's speech, with CoinGlass data showing roughly $481 million in liquidations in the 24 hours around the speech (over $360M from wrongfooted longs). Crypto-adjacent equities (Strategy, Coinbase, Galaxy Digital, Circle) fell 5-8% the same session.
items.actionable: Confirms crypto is trading as a rate-sensitive risk asset this cycle rather than a hedge -- worth re-checking levels before Monday's Asia open given the 24/7 market kept moving over the weekend.

items.headline: Rare earths sell off alongside metals -- MP -4.9%, UUUU -6.8% per the tape, though causation and even magnitude are contested
items.summary: MP Materials and Energy Fuels fell sharply Friday per the code-verified price feed (MP -4.91% to $56.13, UUUU -6.80% to $14.67), likely a mix of the same hawkish-Fed real-yield pressure hitting gold/silver plus AI-capex/semiconductor-sector spillover. One secondary source found UUUU roughly flat the same day -- a genuine, unresolved discrepancy flagged rather than smoothed over. Lynas (ASX, closed before the US session) fell just 0.85%.
items.actionable: Treat Friday's rare-earth move as noisy given the sourcing conflict; the structural China-export-curb and DoD-backing thesis is unaffected either way -- verify live prices before acting on the watchlist.

items.headline: Lynas posts record FY26 revenue (+76% to A$977.9M) but misses profit forecast on rising costs
items.summary: Lynas Rare Earths reported FY26 net profit of A$222.4M (vs A$8M prior year) on record production (REO output +25% to 13,089t, NdPr +11% to 7,260t) and a record average selling price of $80.7/kg, but missed the A$242.5M consensus on rising costs and ramp-up challenges at new Australian facilities. Separately, the Chinese reference NdPr price nearly doubled over twelve months, from $55.00 to $100.80/kg.
items.actionable: The NdPr price near-doubling year-on-year is the structurally bullish read-through for the whole rare-earth watchlist; Lynas's cost overruns are a company-specific execution flag rather than a sector demand problem.

items.headline: Hang Seng closes Friday down 1.1% ahead of the Fed signal; further hawkish-repricing catch-down is a Monday risk
items.summary: Hong Kong's benchmark fell 1.1% (HSCEI -1.02%, Hang Seng Tech -1.77%) Friday, driven by caution ahead of Fed signals and weakness in AI-linked names, closing before Warsh's remarks landed after-hours ET. Xiaomi separately continued under pressure after its Q2 net profit fell 42.6% y/y on pricier memory chips and softer subsidy-driven demand, shares now ~18% below June highs.
items.actionable: HK tech sold off pre-emptively before the actual hawkish shock landed after Asia's close -- Monday's open is a real risk for a further hawkish-repricing catch-down; Xiaomi's margin compression is a separate, company-specific China-tech risk worth tracking apart from the broader HK-tech beta trade.

items.headline: DBS, OCBC post record 1H26 profits; UOB to sell asset-management arm to Allianz GI for S$555M
items.summary: Following 2Q26 results, DBS (S$6.01B net profit, +5%) and OCBC (S$2.22B, +22%, dividend +15%) hit fresh highs, while UOB (S$1.48B, +10%) separately announced selling UOB Asset Management to Allianz Global Investors for S$555M -- expected to lift UOB's CET1 ratio ~14bp and generate a ~S$330M pre-tax gain on completion in 2027. UOB shares had dipped on a rising Greater China NPL ratio and cut fee-income guidance.
items.actionable: Record bank profitability plus a capital-accretive UOB divestment is structurally supportive for the SGX bank book independent of this week's Fed noise, though UOB's Greater China NPL uptick is worth watching separately within the bank sleeve.

items.headline: Hongkong Land's Singapore fund completes ~S$1.1B purchase of Wheelock Place, a positive NAV signpost for SG landlords
items.summary: Hongkong Land's Singapore Central Private Real Estate Fund's acquisition of the Wheelock Place mixed-use property for roughly S$1.1B (US$900M) was expected to complete by end-August, lifting the fund's AUM to S$9.4B -- a large prime-commercial transaction that supports valuation marks across the SG developer/landlord space.
items.actionable: A large prime-asset deal closing this week is a positive NAV signpost for CityDev/UOL/HoBee-style holdings, supporting the SG developer book even as REITs face rate-driven headline pressure from Friday's hawkish Fed surprise.

items.headline: Strait of Hormuz tanker struck, Iran says Oman deal 'not finalized' -- geopolitical risk premium re-enters oil ahead of Sunday reopen
items.summary: UKMTO issued a warning after an oil tanker was hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz near Oman, even as Iran's FM met Qatar's PM in Tehran to discuss reopening the strait; a senior Iranian source told Reuters the Iran-Oman navigational-corridor deal reported earlier in the week has 'not been finalized.' Oil stayed volatile into the weekend, chopping between this de-escalation-reversal and renewed Russia-Ukraine refinery-strike risk.
items.actionable: No direct energy exposure in the book, but the reinstated Hormuz risk premium alongside Russia-Ukraine strike risk is a reminder the geopolitical/inflation angle behind the silver-gold trade hasn't disappeared -- watch Sunday's futures reopen.

items.headline: Global equity funds snap 13-week inflow streak into outflow as gold funds hit a 6-month inflow high
items.summary: LSEG Lipper data for the week ended 26 Aug showed global equity funds posting a -$5.87bn outflow -- the first outflow after 13 straight weeks of inflows -- while gold/precious-metals funds drew +$4.21bn, a 6-month high, and global bond funds added +$10.25bn (a 4-week-low pace). BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator climbed to 9.7, the highest since 2021 and firmly in contrarian-sell territory.
items.actionable: The flow rotation into gold even before Friday's price rout, plus an extremely stretched Bull & Bear reading, both flag a market that was priced for more upside than the fundamentals justified -- consistent with Friday's sharp unwind.

items.headline: Berkshire's Greg Abel resumes buybacks (~$4.5B) and deploys $10B into Alphabet
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway resumed share repurchases (~$4.5B, its first since June 2024) and put roughly $10B of its cash pile to work adding to Alphabet, reported Aug 8-9 -- following the Q2-2026 13F that already showed Berkshire a net equity buyer for the first time in over three years under CEO Greg Abel. Berkshire's cash pile stood at $365.5B as of June 30, down 8% from its record $397.4B.
items.actionable: Confirms Berkshire's Alphabet conviction (also shared by Soros, Druckenmiller and Tiger Global this cycle) extends beyond the 13F snapshot into active buying, plus a genuine capital-return signal via resumed buybacks -- a read on large-allocator risk appetite into September.

items.headline: Ackman launches Pershing Square Ventures, an evergreen fund giving retail access to pre-IPO names
items.summary: Bill Ackman's Pershing Square is launching Pershing Square Ventures, an evergreen fund aimed at giving retail investors pre-IPO access to names in the Anthropic/OpenAI/SpaceX mold -- first reported Aug 13 with expanded coverage through Aug 27. Separate Schedule 13G filings on Pershing Square Inc. itself (dated 14 Aug) show Ackman at 45.3%, Ryan Israel at 7.8% and Pershing Square Management LLC at 75.1% ownership of the holding company.
items.actionable: No direct portfolio read-through, but signals continued institutional appetite for private-market AI/space exposure even as public precious-metals/crypto sold off Friday -- a reminder risk appetite for growth/venture themes remains intact beneath the day's rates story.
